_comment: The scoring model. Rachel places every company on two axes derived only from public investor documents, then reads off a quadrant. Rewrite the anchors for your own market: the axes are the opinionated part, and they should be yours.

anchors.1: No AI mention in the last earnings call or annual report
anchors.3: Dedicated AI commentary, no quantified commitment
anchors.4: Strategic AI narrative with named tools or partners
anchors.5: AI framed as a core moat, CEO-led, quantified

anchors.1-4: That many named, in-production tools publicly confirmed
anchors.5: Five or more confirmed tools, or tools spanning multiple categories as core to the business

compositeFormula: (rhetoric + production) / 2, used for ranking only. The quadrant is the primary read.

quadrants.performer: High rhetoric, confirmed production. Named tools live, quantified ROI. Building compounding advantage.
quadrants.narrative_led: High rhetoric, few confirmed cases. Named programmes and commitments, thin on shipped output.
quadrants.silentBuilder: Low rhetoric, confirmed production. Doing without telling. Underrated.
quadrants.not_visible: Low rhetoric, no confirmed cases. AI absent or incidental in investor materials.

evidenceClasses.confirmed: Named in an earnings transcript, vendor case study, or official press release. Cite the URL.
evidenceClasses.estimated: Strong indirect signal such as a partner listing or job posting. Always labelled as estimated.
evidenceClasses.noEvidence: Absence is disclosed, never hidden and never guessed. Absence is also a signal.
